findings.title: Duplicate self.downsize method shadows earlier definition
findings.body: Two class methods named self.downsize are defined back-to-back: one with signature (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) on lines 145-147 and another with signature (from, to, dimensions, opts) on lines 149-151. In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first; the four-arg overload becomes dead code that is never reachable. The unused definition is misleading and will silently break any other caller that still passes separate width/height integers (those calls would now misroute 200 into the opts hash and raise NoMethodError on opts[:allow_animation]). The dead method should be deleted so only the (from, to, dimensions, opts) form remains.

findings.title: Passing '80%' to gifsicle --resize-fit will fail for animated GIFs
findings.body: The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). The animated branch in resize_instructions_animated assembles `gifsicle <from> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <to>`. gifsicle's --resize-fit expects pixel dimensions of the form WxH; it does not accept a percentage. When allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled and the uploaded image is a GIF, this command will either be rejected by gifsicle or produce no useful output, so the downsize loop's exit-condition (tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes) will never become false and the GIF will be uploaded unmodified (and likely over the size limit).

findings.title: Client-side file-size limit hardcoded to 10 MB and no longer uses SiteSettings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and displayErrorForUpload read `SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`). The PR replaces both with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. The server-side controller still uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (now with an auto-downsize step, but a server-enforced ceiling remains). This decouples client and server validation: an admin who lowers max_image_size_kb below 10 MB will see uploads rejected on the server with a generic 413, while the browser still claims files up to 10 MB are valid; raising max_image_size_kb above 10 MB will not relax the client-side cap. The previous site-setting based values should be restored, or the server limit should also be aligned with 10 MB.

findings.title: Downsize loop does not verify the file is now within the size limit
findings.body: The retry loop only checks `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` before each iteration; if OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (e.g. convert/gifsicle fails, source is unsupported, or the file just can't be compressed enough at 80% scale for five attempts), the loop still exits with attempt reaching 0. The code then unconditionally calls Upload.create_for with `tempfile.size` and creates an Upload record whose underlying file exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. There is no fallback to reject the upload, no log line, and the user gets no error. The loop should re-check size after the downsize call (e.g. re-stat the file) and treat remaining-oversize as an error returned to the caller.
